messages:
Maria L.: quick q about convo endpoint streaming + tool calls — trying to nail down compatible behavior for clients. If a client sends a mix of plain messages and a tool_call, and requests streaming, do we stream partial tool arguments in deltas or only send the full tool payload in the final event?

Example payload client might send:```json
{
  \"model\": \"rwd-2.0\",
  \"messages\": [
    {\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"search for restaurants\"},
    {\"role\": \"assistant\", \"tool_call\": {\"name\": \"search_api\", \"arguments\": \"{\\\"q\\\": \\\"sushi near me\\\"}\"}}
  ],
  \"stream\": true
}
```

Would love a short spec we can point clients at. cc @Kevin B.

Kevin B.: short answer: current runtime streams deltas for tool calls as plain text fragments (we were treating arguments like regular content). That caused clients to reassemble freeform, which is messy.

Kevin B.: proposal: emit a delta envelope for tool calls with typed chunks, e.g. `{"delta_type":"tool_call","name":"search_api","args_fragment":"..."}` and then a final chunk `{"delta_type":"tool_call_complete","name":"search_api","args":"{...}"}` so clients can reassemble deterministically.

Sophie R.: that sounds safer. but for backward compat we should default to the legacy behavior unless client opts in with a flag like `stream_tool_calls: true` — avoids breaking older SDKs.

Tim (eng): agree with Sophie. can we make the opt-in flag `stream_tool_calls=true` and also include a `tool_call_id` GUID on deltas so multiple concurrent tool calls in a single stream don't interleave incorrectly?

Kevin B.: yes — `tool_call_id` + `args_fragment` + `is_final` boolean is simplest. pseudocode chunks:```json
{\"delta_type\":\"tool_call\",\"tool_call_id\":\"abc123\",\"name\":\"search_api\",\"args_fragment\":\"{\\\"q\\\": \\\"su\"}
{\"delta_type\":\"tool_call\",\"tool_call_id\":\"abc123\",\"args_fragment\":\"shi near me\"}
{\"delta_type\":\"tool_call_complete\",\"tool_call_id\":\"abc123\",\"name\":\"search_api\",\"args\":\"{\\\"q\\\": \\\"sushi near me\\\"}\"}```

Maria L.: sounds good. for API contract doc: we should add migration note that servers without `stream_tool_calls` will continue to stream raw argument text (legacy) until opt-in is used. also call out server behavior when `stream=true` but `stream_tool_calls=false` — only final tool_call event in non-delta friendly envelope.

Sophie R.: +1. Also add a small parsing example for JS SDK showing how to assemble fragments using `tool_call_id`.

Tim (eng): I'll make a tiny RFC and open a PR against the docs repo. linking draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/412 (WIP) — will add examples and a compatibility table.

Kevin B.: fyi runtime change required: streaming layer needs to tag tool call fragments and surface `tool_call_id`. I'll add unit tests and a fallback that emits final-only when `stream_tool_calls` is absent.

Maria L.: sweet. can someone add a short note in the API changelog about clients needing opt-in for structured tool deltas? that'll help SDKs.

Tim (eng): will do. @Sophie R. can you review the doc PR when I push?

Sophie R.: yes, will review. quick ask: should we also include `tool_call_error` delta for partial failures? e.g., runtime cannot serialize args mid-stream.

Kevin B.: good call — include `tool_call_error` with `tool_call_id` and `message`. clients should treat that as terminal for that call.

ci-bot: build passed for PR #412 :white_check_mark: (job 8742)

Maria L.: awesome, thanks team. i'll follow up next week if we need any contract wording tweaks. :thumbsup:
